key_insight: Weak periodic forcing barely changes the mean jet, but it strongly reshapes turbulence scales and increases inertial-particle clustering in phase-dependent ways.
engineering_relevance: This suggests low-frequency actuation can be used to control particle dispersion and agglomeration in jets without major changes to the bulk flow.
method: Turbulent planar jet studied at two Reynolds numbers: about 4950 and 9900.
Sinusoidal forcing applied at a frequency far below the natural jet instability.
Hot-wire anemometry and high-speed particle imaging used with Voronoi tessellations to quantify clustering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 40% reduction in integral scale and 21–49% cycle-dependent changes in preferential concentration, while the time-averaged mean-flow relationship remains nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The forcing is weak and low-frequency, so these results may not transfer directly to stronger actuation or different jet geometries/particle loadings.
paper_title: Preferential concentration in a periodically forced particle-laden turbulent planar jet
